notes.note-1: IPC to extensions is HTTP POST, not WebSocket (decision D1). All calls go to 127.0.0.1 only.
notes.note-2: Extension secrets stored via M-019 datacenter keychain. Never build a separate secret store.
notes.note-3: New commands mt_ext_* require: generate_handler! + tauri.v2.json fixture + m001_validate::REGISTERED_COMMANDS updates.
notes.note-4: Extensibility test: design must support a second hypothetical extension beyond TokMo without code changes.
notes.note-5: Live-doc wire contract v2 (breaking): /stream/open sends sections as an ordered array of {name, content} with real initial content; document_md is the authoritative join of sections (initial_md advisory). /stream/patch carries op: "append" | "replace" ("replace_section" accepted as synonym, missing op defaults to "replace"); section content is self-contained markdown — Mark never adds headers; unknown op or unknown section is rejected with 400. Document rebuild is deterministic: declared section order, empty sections skipped, "\n\n" separator. Recovery: /stream/open with the SAME session_id on an active session replaces state wholesale (resync path, log BLOCK_DOC_OPEN_RESYNC) — the escape hatch for a client stuck on needs_resync; a DIFFERENT session_id still gets 409. TokMo is the only consumer; both apps ship together.

M-046.Name: ReleasePreflight
M-046.Summary:
C-RELEASE-PIPELINE-AUTOMATION (2026-10-20): M-046 now owns the repository release train authority, release preparation and atomic JSON/Markdown train-ledger plus version normalization, exact README/CHANGELOG/release-note/What's New material checks, payload-to-seal readiness, the public one-way Project mirror, owner-local GitHub control reconciliation, input-free owner-approved annotated-tag promotion, tag-only signing, read-only publication-bundle preparation, fixed-command digest-verified draft-first publication, and an idempotent downstream cask handoff. C-RELEASE-PIPELINE-CLOSEOUT records the public Project identity, activates the reviewed main/tag rulesets, and extends the cask handoff with tap-owned validation plus exact-bot-PR auto-merge behind the required check; Projects remains a non-authoritative one-way mirror. Tag admission restores the remote annotated tag object after checkout rewrites its local tag ref to the peeled commit, then proves the restored object targets the checked-out seal before packaging. Promotion preserves complete main ancestry before both strict admission passes so payload-to-seal merge-base evidence is available on hosted runners. C-RELEASE-CONVEYOR (2026-10-24): Release Please is retired — package.json, set by npm version in the reviewed preparation PR, is the single version authority and normalization propagates it; the current train is named once in docs/release-trains/current.json and resolved by tools/release-train.mjs; the payload-to-seal span may hold any number of bookkeeping-only commits (each proven, merges judged against their first parent); promotion binds to a seal that is on main rather than main's exact tip; publication itself proves the releases/latest feed advanced. Manual dispatch is unsigned build-only; Projects never becomes gate authority; secrets and admin apply are isolated by purpose. The pull-request Tauri dry-run also remains unprivileged: it disables updater artifacts through a narrow CLI config override while retaining .app/DMG packaging, ad-hoc signing, install smoke, size and warning evidence. Production tag builds keep updater artifacts enabled and receive the updater private key only inside release-signing. Retained synthetic preference JSON and its manifest use LF checkout bytes; privacy verification normalizes host path separators and accepts manifest line delimiters on Windows, macOS and Linux.
C-ACCEPTANCE-REGISTRY (2026-10-21): M-046 admission gains an ordered evidence trail — docs/acceptance/registry.json registers every isolated test artifact (source sha, bundle identity, binary digest, build recipe via tools/build-test-artifact.mjs) and every review wave and owner verdict per delivery item; tools/acceptance-registry.mjs --check enforces schema, git sha resolvability and two-way consistency with the collecting train inside the standard vitest matrix (V-M-046). vitest.int.config.mjs re-exports the canonical Vitest configuration for portable historical C-71 commands, without machine-specific paths. C-FIX-013: the canonical vitest config guards Node >= 25 default-on experimental Web Storage with a conditional test.execArgv (--no-experimental-webstorage, passed only on major >= 25 so the Node 22 reference runtime keeps byte-identical worker arguments) so the jsdom localStorage implementation stays authoritative; .nvmrc pins the Node 22 reference runtime. The test workflow gates session restore and close/edit ownership in WKWebView's browser engine through webkit-session. The test workflow also gates C-68 diff priority/opened-baseline regressions through the webkit-diff project. The test workflow gates native Shift+Up/Down selection with the passive format toolbar through the webkit-keyboard project. C-63: the test workflow explicitly gates the C-60 footnote and C-62 diagram-appearance projects in WebKit after browser installation, preserving their WKWebView-engine coverage on every test run. Provide a deterministic pre-publication gate for exact version/tag consistency, complete automated verification, and signed/notarized macOS artifact evidence. C-15 T-106: the release workflow gained a windows-x64 NSIS lane (silent-install smoke, size budget, per-platform updater-feed fragments merged at publish) staged behind the WINDOWS_RELEASE repo variable until manual QA passes; test.yml runs renderer+backend units on windows-latest as the Windows-cfg compile gate.
C-RELEASE-MANUAL-PUBLISH (2026-10-26) repealed the C-RELEASE-TIMING publication mechanic: the veto-window job (RELEASE_VETO_MINUTES, cancel-as-veto, the optional release-notify Telegram ping) is gone, and publication waits for the owner to approve the synchronous release Environment — the release-authorize approval creates the tag (the first explicit owner instruction), the release-Environment approval publishes (the final one), so nothing goes live by silence (owner train rule 1). Kept C-RELEASE-TIMING legacy: the release build lane no longer re-runs the payload suites (vitest, cargo test, playwright) already proven green on the exact payload by strict admission's status-check aggregate; tauri's beforeBuildCommand builds the renderer, and typecheck:ipc stays lane-local. cargo-bundle-licenses and cargo-cyclonedx binaries are cached, and the cargo build cache is keyed on Cargo.lock only so incremental rebuilds stay warm.
C-PUBLIC-REPOSITORY-HYGIENE (2026-10-24): the portable release runbook lives in docs/release-process.md; AGENTS.md routes to it and the release-train protocol links to it directly without changing release admission or publication behavior.
C-RELEASE-LEDGER-GUARD (2026-10-27): readiness validates the human Markdown ledger against the JSON authority for item membership as well as the state/version header — every admitted or excluded item id must appear as a whole id (C-1 is not satisfied by C-10), so an admission that edits only the JSON fails closed with MT_RELEASE_LEDGER_DRIFT.

notes.note-4: While the embedded endpoint uses GitHub `/releases/latest`, shipped beta tags must be created and idempotently updated with `prerelease=false`; SemVer still carries the `-beta` channel label.
notes.note-5: The Homebrew cask publication gate must prove its URL template resolves to `Mark_#{version}_aarch64.dmg`, matching the staged and published Tauri asset.
notes.note-6: The native title-path clipboard and layout-independent undo repair releases as v2.1.3-beta and doubles as the first real installed-client verification of the signed v2.1.2-beta in-app updater.

M-053.Name: SiteBuild
M-053.Summary: VitePress site with the marketing landing emitted at the root and the diagram gallery at /diagrams/ (C-58) by buildEnd hooks (both served by dev middlewares), env-driven SITE_URL/SITE_BASE, a shared per-page SEO/OG head, sitemap/robots/CNAME, opt-in cookieless Umami analytics, a dist link checker that also gates the gallery page, and a single GitHub Pages workflow (PR build+check, main deploy). The gallery renders site/gallery/examples.mjs through pele at build time into inline SVGs recoloured live by --pele-* variables derived from the app's own theme CSS via muya's buildPeleVariables (site/gallery/theme-vars.json, regenerated on every build). Since C-64 T-001 the site wears one brand: site/shared/brand.css is the single token source (paper/ink/marker, light+dark, self-hosted Bricolage/Plex faces under /fonts/brand/), the docs theme (site/.vitepress/theme) extends DefaultTheme over it, and the shared no-flash theme-init script keeps docs, gallery and landing on one VitePress-storage-key choice. C-64 T-002 rebuilds the landing itself as the mobile-first page per D-9: a draggable before/after hero (raw agent Markdown versus Mark's rendered page, diagrams injected at build time into DIAGRAM placeholders with theme data from THEME_VARS_JSON), the d1 four-fact strip, the d2 diagram wall as section 02 with live theme chips, install cards carrying the verified facts (v2.5.0, App Store id, full brew command, Windows setup.exe), an iOS/iPadOS Mark-for-Mac sticky bar (Web Share with copy fallback, remembered dismiss, share_to_mac events) and download_click hooks on every install CTA; tests/site/landing-content.test.mjs pins the contract. C-64 T-003 adds the SEO/consent/security layer: the shared head carries apple-itunes-app, the brand theme-color pair, strict referrer, hreflang en + x-default, the 1200x630 og-card.png and a JSON-LD @graph (SoftwareApplication with softwareVersion from the root package.json + WebSite; docs pages get docsHeadTags with WebSite only); GA4 loads consent.js (Consent Mode v2, geo gate, card shown only after the [data-consent-after] hero leaves the viewport) plus track.js (consent-gated download_click / outbound_click / kofi_click, one-shot guide doc_read at 75% depth, and share_to_mac / snippet_copy / diagram_copy / diagram_filter via window.markTrack). GA configuration strips the URL hash and non-campaign query fields, preserves only named UTM values, and reduces referrers to their origin. VitePress owns SITE_BASE application for theme-nav routes; full-navigation links from guide content stay base-agnostic. buildEnd also emits llms.txt and .well-known/security.txt (site/scripts/seo-files.mjs) and rewrites every built page with a meta CSP pinning each inline script by its exact-content sha256 (site/scripts/csp.mjs: cspFor / injectCsp / applyCsp / verifyCsp; check-dist fails on a tampered script); site/scripts/og-card.mjs regenerates the OG card PNG from site/og/card.html with Playwright.

Interface.fn-appVersion: memoized root package.json version (one source for softwareVersion)
Interface.fn-sharedHeadTags: settings + page {path,title,description} -> shared head HTML (SEO set + JSON-LD + analytics)
Interface.fn-docsHeadTags: settings -> VitePress HeadConfig list (banner, theme pair, referrer, WebSite JSON-LD)
Interface.fn-jsonLd: settings + page -> JSON-LD @graph body with '<' escaped
Interface.fn-renderPage: template + settings + page meta -> servable static page
Interface.fn-deriveThemeVars: app theme CSS files -> gallery theme table (16 --pele-* keys + page + dark per theme)
Interface.fn-renderGallery: settings -> /diagrams/ page (build-time pele SVGs, theme strip, slideshow, fullscreen show)
Interface.fn-checkDist: fail the build on unresolved internal links, leftover tokens, or an incomplete gallery page
Interface.fn-THEME_INIT_JS: theme-init.js contents as a string — the no-flash head script shared by docs head config, the gallery and (later) the landing
Interface.var-brandCss: site/shared/brand.css tokens — the single source of the site look, imported by the docs theme and inlined into the gallery build
Interface.fn-llmsTxt: settings -> llms.txt body (install paths + docs map, absolute URLs)
Interface.fn-cspFor: html + analytics -> meta CSP string with a sha256 per inline script, provider hosts toggled by config
Interface.fn-injectCsp: html + opts -> html with the CSP meta as the first child of head (idempotent)
Interface.fn-applyCsp: outDir + opts -> rewrite every built .html with its policy, {files, hashes}
Interface.fn-verifyCsp: html -> inline script hashes missing from the page's own CSP meta
Interface.fn-checkDist: fail the build on unresolved internal links, leftover tokens, an incomplete gallery page, a missing/broken SEO set, or an unpinned inline script
Interface.fn-windowMarkTrack: name + params -> consent-gated GA4 event with an in-memory pre-decision queue
Interface.fn-gaPageLocation: window.location -> GA4 page URL containing only origin, path and named UTM parameters

M-064.Name: RepositorySafetyGate
M-064.Summary:
C-PUBLIC-REPOSITORY-HYGIENE keeps the public gate deterministic and portable. It snapshots exact staged trees, commit messages, outgoing commits and ref updates; rejects reserved/private paths, credentials, personal absolute paths, private infrastructure, unsupported binaries, unsafe lane crossings, AI attribution and AI-prefixed branch names; runs Gitleaks with trusted defaults; rebuilds the candidate identity after the scan; and stores a private hash-bound receipt in the common Git directory.
C-SAFE-SCREENSHOT-REVIEW admits only regular README PNG bytes whose exact SHA-256 identity and completed human visual review are present in a changed release screenshot manifest in the same commit. Outgoing commits are evaluated independently; every other binary stays blocked. Deletion-only branch housekeeping is admitted only for non-main tips proven merged into remote main. C-MESSAGE-ONLY-HISTORY-REWRITE-V3 adds a message-only main rewrite lane bound to an exact owner-local manifest. It proves paired ordered-parent DAGs and raw headers, preserves every tree and identity, and permits only approved message replacements plus the explicitly counted removal of GPG signatures invalidated by new commit identities. Its recovery phase admits a single desktop PR rebase only when the live old branch tip and live main read from the actual push endpoint match the negotiated and remote-tracking identities, the new head descends from that main, and every replayed commit unique to the rebuilt branch passes the normal push scan. The endpoint is never retained in review payloads, receipts or diagnostics.
C-SAFETY-GATE-MODEL-REVIEW restores the exact-candidate model review as two serial local model passes and one independent non-local pass. Both reviewers must pass every chunk; endpoints and model names come from owner-local configuration outside the repository, the non-local endpoint must resolve to a private or overlay address, and an unreachable or unsafe reviewer fails closed. An explicit human MARK_SAFETY_OVERRIDE skips only the model phase and writes an identity-bound private receipt. The deterministic boundary also rejects owner-workspace and private-companion references.

Contract.Purpose: Stop a local commit or push unless the exact complete candidate passes deterministic exposure, lane, Gitleaks and identity checks plus two serial local model passes and one independent non-local model pass, including manifest-bound screenshot evidence, exact-manifest proof for an approved message-only main rewrite, and push-endpoint live-tip/current-main proof for a rebuilt desktop PR branch.

Input.Name: candidate
Input.Type: staged tree/message, independently grouped outgoing commits, a push-endpoint/current-main-bound desktop PR rebase, or paired raw commit DAGs plus an owner-local rewrite manifest

Output.Name: decision
Output.Type: pass or fail with redacted markers and private hash-bound evidence

Error.Description: Exposure, private-companion reference, incomplete evidence, unsupported payload, changed candidate, missing, unreachable, public, redirecting, slot-ambiguous or non-passing model reviewer, stale or shallow history, missing push endpoint, stale branch/main identity, unbased desktop PR rebase, rewrite manifest/DAG/header/signature mismatch, an unproven branch deletion, AI attribution, or an AI-named branch.

M-065.Name: ExportImagesEmbed
M-065.Summary: The styledHtml export pass that makes the exported .html self-contained: img src values resolve against the exporting document's directory (muya exports relative images as absolute file:// URLs; drive-letter and \\?\ extended-prefix forms are isWin-gated correctImageSrc semantics re-expressed locally), percent-encoding decodes, ipcFs.stat gates each distinct path at the 8 MiB per-image cap without a read, and ipcFs.readBinary (the lossless channel — window.fileUtils.readFile returns UTF-8 text and corrupts binary) base64-embeds the bytes with an extension-mapped MIME. Remote http(s) and existing data: URLs are never fetched or rewritten; generic UNC, unknown extensions and missing/over-cap/unreadable files keep their src and count as skipped references; an untitled document passes relative src through uncounted. Accounting counts references, reads dedupe by resolved path. C-SELF-CONTAINED-HTML-EXPORT wires it into the styledHtml branch of editor.vue handleExport only — pdf/print containers resolve src themselves at print time.
M-065.Dependencies: M-013-B ipcFs (stat, readBinary); arrayBufferToBase64 from src/renderer/src/util/fileSystem.js; isWindows from src/renderer/src/util/index.js; called by the styledHtml branch of editor.vue handleExport

Contract.Purpose: Turn the generated styled-HTML export into a single self-contained file by embedding local images as data-URLs, without ever fetching remote content or failing the export on an image.

Input.Name: baseDir
Input.Type: string|null — exporting document's directory (null for untitled)

Output.Name: result
Output.Type: { html, embedded, total, skipped } — html differs from the input only in img src values

Error.Description: missing, over-cap, unreadable or unknown-extension local images keep their original src; the caller warns with embedded/total counts

M-066.Name: ExportDocxConverter
M-066.Summary: The renderer-side Word converter (C-NATIVE-DOCX-RTF-EXPORT): muya's styled export HTML (the same exportStyledHTML output the HTML export uses) passes the M-065 embed pass in the caller, then a data-only pre-pass strips the pre.front-matter block, adapts muya's class/role footnote markup to the data-footnote-* shape docx/html recognizes, and replaces exportable figures (C-56 roles) with rasterized 2x PNG images in document order. The lazy docx + docx/html dynamic import (check-export-chunk guard: entry chunk clean, docx surface 107.6 KB gzip measured, 300 KB budget) converts with htmlToContent in the document's own named styles; sectPr geometry comes from the remembered print options (m052-mirrored mm mapping, landscape handled by the library). Writing rides the existing binary facade (mt_fs_write_binary) — no new commands, no print surface. The success notification carries reveal + quiet "Export settings" actions (C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM API). Enabling muya fact: EXPORT_DOMPURIFY_CONFIG mathMl now true, so KaTeX's MathML twin survives export and feeds native OMML equations (T-002 discovery; screen-reader parity bonus). Known input gap (backlog): muya's export grammar renders $$ display blocks as literal text — inline math converts today, display math joins when that muya fix lands.
M-066.Dependencies: M-065 embedLocalImages (runs before, in editor.vue); muya ExportHtml (renderHtml) and muya/lib/utils/diagramExport (figure raster); docx + docx/html via dynamic import; store/editor.js _EXPORT_DOCX (save dialog + write + notify); m009_menu.rs file.export-file-docx; commands file.export-file-docx; contextMenu/tabs export group

Contract.Purpose: Turn the styled export HTML into a real .docx buffer — native OMML equations from KaTeX MathML, real footnotes, native checkboxes, named Word styles — without any modal, print surface or new backend command.

Input.Name: html
Input.Type: string — muya exportStyledHTML output after the M-065 pass

Error.Description: caller notifies editor.export.failed; nothing is written

M-067.Name: NotificationCardSystem
M-067.Summary: The unified notification system (C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM): one card renderer (icon-chip variant — chromeIcons glyph in a 14% severity-tint circle, C-66 card metrics, float/editor/button theme tokens, severity tokens --notifyInfo/Success/ Warning/Error in all 34 themes) over a pinia store owning the live stack (max 3 rendered cards + overflow chip with per-locale plurals, hover-pause timers, sticky errors, Esc-topmost) and the session history (FIFO cap 50, palette command view.notifications-history, full untruncated text, per-entry copy). The legacy Fluent DOM toast service became a compatibility facade forwarding the same notify()/clear() call shape (~70 call sites untouched) plus the new event fields: severity x source (file/export/project/update/agent/system), actions[] (copy/retry/open/reveal built-ins + custom label+handler, primary/normal/quiet styles, no-answer-owed contract replacing showConfirm promises), dedupKey collapsing with xN counters, sticky. Copy-on-select on cards and the reskinned per-file banner: selection release writes exactly the selection; the only confirmation is the selection double-pulsing green (no label). The C-66 update notice injects its three actions as a sticky info entry — semantics untouched.
M-067.Dependencies: M-057 chromeIcons (severity glyphs); pinia; i18n (ten locales); bus; element-plus dialog (history); consumed by store/notification.js facade, store/editor.js call sites, components/updateNotice, components/editorWithTabs/notifications.vue

Contract.Purpose: Every transient app message renders as one severity-styled card in one stack, is recoverable from the session history, offers only shortcut actions that owe no answer, and lets developers copy any notification text by selecting it.

Input.Name: NOTIFY payload
Input.Type: { severity, source, title, message, actions, dedupKey, sticky, time } — legacy {type} maps primary→info, unknown→info

Output.Name: stack/history state
Output.Type: live entries (max 3 rendered + overflow counter) and FIFO history entries {time, severity, source, title, fullText}

Error.Description: copy-on-select and copy actions silently no-op — a quiet developer feature never surfaces an error
